claims.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
claims.claim: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA within 15 minutes once it knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving a death of an individual at the mine.
claims.quote:
The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

(a) A death of an individual at the mine;
claims.reason: The quote directly states the operator must contact MSHA within 15 minutes once it knows or should know of an accident involving a death at the mine, matching the claim exactly.

claims.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
claims.claim: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent
claims.reason: The quote directly states the incombustible content of combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent, matching the claim exactly.

claims.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
claims.claim: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground, and to visitors authorized to enter the mine by the operator, an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.reason: The quote explicitly states operators must provide each miner an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer, matching the claim exactly.

claims.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
claims.claim: The requirement is met by a 1-hour SCSR, or an SCSR of not less than 10 minutes plus a 1-hour canister, or other self-contained breathing apparatus providing protection for 1 hour or longer.
claims.reason: The quote lists the same three options (1-hour SCSR, SCSR of not less than 10 minutes plus 1-hour canister, or other self-contained breathing apparatus providing 1 hour or longer protection) that the claim states.

claims.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
claims.claim: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.
claims.reason: The quote is identical to the claim, word for word.

claims.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
claims.claim: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training before such miner is assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.
claims.reason: The quote states verbatim that each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties, matching the claim exactly.

claims.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
claims.claim: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.
claims.reason: The quote matches the claim word-for-word, defining the permissible exposure level exactly as stated.

claims.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
claims.claim: Berms or guardrails shall be provided and maintained on the banks of roadways where a drop-off exists of sufficient grade or depth to cause a vehicle to overturn or endanger persons in equipment.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be provided and maintained on the banks of roadways where a drop-off exists of sufficient grade or depth to cause a vehicle to overturn or endanger persons in equipment.
claims.reason: The quote supports that berms/guardrails must be provided where drop-offs exist, but it does not state any specific height requirement, which is what the question asks.

claims.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
claims.claim: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway (56.9300).
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.reason: The quote states verbatim that berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment usually traveling the roadway, matching the claim exactly.

claims.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
claims.claim: The same mid-axle height requirement applies under 57.9300 for underground metal and nonmetal mines.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.reason: The quote states the mid-axle height requirement but does not mention section 57.9300 or specify that it applies to underground mines.

claims.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
claims.claim: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,
